assumptions.what: The paper's transmission probabilities and posterior distributions are read from the figures; only the medians and 95% intervals are printed. All of these are MCMC output, so posterior quantities are compared at a Monte Carlo tolerance (recorded per field), not at printed precision. Reported medians and intervals are pooled over four independent chains of 100,000 iterations each, shown to have converged (R-hat < 1.01, high ESS); see the convergence items. Our figures are drawn at the published figure's pixel size with the same panel layout and axis ranges.
assumptions.sensitivity: Medians move by about one unit and interval ends by several units between seeds; see the per-field tolerances.

cause.summary: The paper deposited no seed and no data for the simulated test outbreak, so this is a fresh realization of the same model, not the same dataset. The specific map and dot pattern therefore differ by construction; the panels are drawn on the published pixel grid and histogram axes for comparison. What the paper reports for Fig. 2 reproduces: the tree misses at most a couple of the 20 transmissions, and the true mean latency and mean transmission distance fall inside the 95% intervals.

check.detail: 4 chains x 50000: max R-hat 1.004, min ESS 671, most-likely-source agreement 1.0, max transmission-prob diff 0.062

cause.summary: Four independent chains of 100,000 iterations each converge on the simulated outbreak: R-hat below 1.01 on every continuous parameter. The chains recover the known mean latency and mean transmission distance (both true values fall inside the pooled 95% intervals) and the known transmission relationships; the most-likely tree is less unanimous across chains than for the real data, as expected for a dense 20-premise simulation with several near-equal sources.

cause.summary: Four independent chains of 100,000 iterations each (400,000 total, within a factor of the paper's 500,000) converge: R-hat below 1.01 on every continuous parameter, effective sample sizes in the thousands, and the chains agree on the most-likely source of almost every premise. The reported medians, intervals and figure are pooled over the four chains.

fields.name: K is the hub (max out-degree premise)

assumptions.what: The paper's transmission probabilities and posterior distributions are read from the figures; only the medians and 95% intervals are printed. All of these are MCMC output, so posterior quantities are compared at a Monte Carlo tolerance (recorded per field), not at printed precision. Reported medians and intervals are pooled over four independent chains of 100,000 iterations each, shown to have converged (R-hat < 1.01, high ESS); see the convergence items. Our figures are drawn at the published figure's pixel size with the same panel layout and axis ranges.
assumptions.sensitivity: Medians move by about one unit and interval ends by several units between seeds; see the per-field tolerances.

cause.summary: The highest-posterior tree reproduces the paper's K-hub scenario with the two longer chains, and the 24-day median latency. Our single most-likely labelled tree holds a smaller share of the posterior than the paper's reported >99%, because the better-mixing sampler splits probability across trees that differ only in one leaf's parent; grouped by the K-hub scenario the share is far higher.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The gap is a tree-labelling effect: near-identical K-hub trees share the posterior mass
hypotheses.test: Compare the exact-tree probability with the probability of the K-hub scenario class (K as max out-degree)

hypotheses.hypothesis: The gap is under-convergence of the chain
hypotheses.test: Latency and distance medians and the K-hub structure are stable across seeds and iteration counts

check.detail: 4 chains x 100000: max R-hat 1.001, min ESS 5854, most-likely-source agreement 1.0, max transmission-prob diff 0.037

cause.summary: Four independent chains of 100,000 iterations each converge: R-hat below 1.01 on every continuous parameter and high effective sample sizes. The K-hub structure is stable across all four chains; the single most-likely labelled tree holds a smaller share of the posterior than the paper's reported >99% because near-identical K-hub trees split the mass, which the convergence diagnostics confirm is not a mixing artifact.

cause.summary: Fig. S14 is a statistical-parsimony network built with the external TCS program (ref 16), a separate tool not part of this method; not reproduced.

The 100-premise run took about a month of compute in 2012 at 5e5 iterations; it is out of the CI budget and was not run. The 20-premise simulation (Fig. 2) and the two real-data analyses exercise the same method.
evidence: Text S1; paper reports ~1 month of compute

hypotheses.hypothesis: A scaled-down 100-premise run would fit the pull-request CI budget
hypotheses.test: One 100-premise chain at I=100 costs O(I^3) per genetic evaluation; even a short chain is far over 30 minutes on a standard runner

hypotheses.hypothesis: The method does not scale to 100 premises at all
hypotheses.test: The simulator and sampler run at I=100; only the wall-clock is prohibitive here
